\title{Find vs.\ Fix: Does Locating a Shortcut Inside a Language Model Tell Us Where to Repair It?}

\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Sonu Akash, Sidhant Holla, Siddhant Khurdiya, Piyush Shiv}
\IEEEauthorblockA{Department of Computer Science and Engineering (AI \& ML)\\
PES University, Bengaluru, India}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Interpretability tools can locate where a behaviour acts inside a language model, but prior work on factual knowledge
found that this location need not be where an edit works best. We ask the same question for a shortcut learned during
fine-tuning, in a controlled setting with known ground truth. GPT-2 small is fine-tuned for IMDB sentiment
classification with an invented actor name planted in 5\% of the training reviews, one name always on positive and
another always on negative reviews; every model has a matched clean twin and three seeds, and the main analyses and
their decision rules were fixed before each run. The logit lens, block swaps and activation patching agree that the shortcut is \emph{built early but used
late}: the true sentiment is still readable at layer~9 on reviews whose name points the wrong way, and the name's effect
reaches the answer position only in blocks 9--11. Retraining \emph{any} single block on clean data removes the shortcut,
but an ablation shows why: the clean data contains the names with both labels, and without these counter-examples no
block fixes it. Location therefore does not tell us where to retrain. It does matter for a training-free fix: reading
the answer out at the layer the tools identify, an early exit implemented inside the forward pass, removes
\pSixBEqLNineRemovedFullFT{} of the shortcut at equal dose, against at most \pSixBEqLSixRemovedFullFTsTwo{} from early
layers, while a random vector under the same accuracy limit removes \pSixBRandomRemovedFullFT. We replicate the analysis
with LoRA and Pythia-160M, where the tools place the shortcut early, and contrast it with memorized wrong labels.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
shortcut learning, interpretability, logit lens, activation patching, fine-tuning, LoRA, GPT-2, pre-registration
\end{IEEEkeywords}
